data.narrative:
Cylib is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Lilian Schwich, Gideon Schwich, and Paul Sabarny. The target operates within a sector populated by 9 private peers (including Helion, Redwood Materials, and QuantumScape) and 1 public comparable (LNZA). The company has raised €140M+ to date, comprising a €55M Series A tranche plus €26.1M in NRW grant funding and €63.4M in BMWE grant funding.

Valuation analysis relied on the stage-progression method, which applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement to the €140M+ total raised proxy, yielding an implied valuation of €280M. A peer-median approach was not applicable due to insufficient narrow-filter comparables in the Climate & Energy sector; while nine same-sector peers exist, none satisfied same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier filters needed for robust triangulation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of €238M to €322M, centered on €280M. This single-method conclusion carries material execution risk: the absence of tight peer comparables limits cross-validation, and actual post-Series A pricing will depend heavily on operational milestones, capital deployment efficiency, and sector-specific funding momentum. Additional uncertainty stems from the substantial proportion of non-dilutive grant capital (€89.5M of €140M+), which may not correspond directly to market-priced equity value.
